name: Kazimierz Brodziński
credit: Portrait of Kazimierz Brodziński, from Henryk Piątkowski, Album pisarzy polskich (1898) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Kazimierz Brodziński (1791–1835) was born at Królówka near Bochnia, in the Kraków region, and grew up in the Galician countryside whose peasant life he later made his subject. He served in the army of the Duchy of Warsaw in 1809 and afterwards worked as a teacher and critic in Warsaw, where he became a professor at the university in 1822.

He is the chief Polish poet of sentimentalism and a critic who helped open the way for Romanticism in his country. His idyll Wiesław (1820), a tale of Cracovian villagers, was widely loved for its gentle picture of peasant virtue. After the November Uprising of 1830–31 he went into exile and died in Dresden in 1835. John Bowring included him in his Specimens of the Polish Poets (1827). The works here are Wiesław in the original Polish and in Bowring's English verse.
